title: DR1 asks for a CPH number on every consignment except horses and the 01061900 group; the frontend asks only when the consignment contains cattle.

finding.frontend: The CPH row appears on the addresses hub, and the CPH page is reachable, only when a commodity line matches a whitelist of one entry: `CPH_COMMODITIES = ['Cow']` (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:119, applied by src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/cph-number/controller.js:27-30 and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/controller.js:50-52). Everything else in the catalogue — horses, cats, dogs and fish — is never asked for a CPH number. The rule is an allow-list, so every commodity added to the catalogue from now on defaults to not being asked.
finding.prototype: DR1 works the opposite way round: the CPH section is in the default set of address sections, and a commodity code has to be listed explicitly to escape it (app/data/consignment-address-sections.js:148-160). Two live-animal codes escape — 0101, horses, and 01061900, the cat/dog/ferret group, which gets a permanent-address section instead (:101,124). Cattle and pigs are listed explicitly with CPH included (:108,116), and every other live-animal code in DR1's catalogue, from sheep and goats through poultry to ornamental fish, falls to the default and is asked for one. Two germinal-product codes, 05111000 and 05119985, are also listed without CPH (:132,139), but germinal products are outside this comparison, so they neither add to nor subtract from the rule for live animals.
finding.difference: Invert the rule: ask for a CPH number unless the consignment's commodity is one that is exempt, and make the exempt list horses and the 01061900 group rather than making cattle the only inclusion. Within today's five-entry catalogue this changes one commodity, fish, which DR1 asks and the frontend does not; the reason to do it anyway is that the allow-list makes every future commodity silently exempt, which is the wrong default for a question DR1 treats as the norm. Whether each newly-included commodity really needs a CPH number is a question for the catalogue work rather than for this rule.
finding.falsifiedBy: A live-animal commodity code in DR1's catalogue, outside 0101 and 01061900, that is not asked for a CPH number, which would mean the default set is incidental rather than the rule.
finding.correction: Claim corrected, finding stands. It said only two commodity codes escape the CPH default. Four do: 0101 and 01061900 as claimed, and also 05111000 and 05119985. Checked by reading the whole code-to-sections map rather than the two entries the finding named. The two extra codes are germinal products — semen, embryos and ova — which the finding contract puts outside this comparison, so the rule the finding describes holds for every live-animal code in DR1's catalogue: 0102 and 0103 name CPH explicitly, and 010410, 010420, the 01051x poultry range, 010613, 010614, 010620, 010632, 010633, 01064100 and 030111 all fall to the default and get it. The prototype slot and the falsifier are amended to say live-animal, because as originally written the falsifier fired on the finding's own evidence. The frontend half needed no change: the allow-list really is one entry, `CPH_COMMODITIES = ['Cow']`, and the frontend's fish carries code 0301, which under DR1's rule falls to the default and is asked — so the one-commodity blast radius inside today's catalogue is right. The medium confidence is right too: with five commodities in the catalogue the rule itself cannot be watched working, only read. One caution about how it is argued: "invert the allow-list" is a statement about the shape of the rule rather than about what a user meets, and a finding whose substance is a code difference is not a finding. This one survives because it has a user-facing core underneath — a trader importing ornamental fish is asked for a CPH number in DR1 and is not asked in the frontend — and that is the sentence to lead with when the work is picked up.

relatedTo.why: how much the rule change matters depends on how far the catalogue grows past its five entries
